doc.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Moving The Rag online
summary: Johnson explains the move to online publication: post office problems, costs, health, and the first online issue and reformatting.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It must have been a major decision to go to on-line publication. Is that something you had prepared for or thought about for a long time?
Well I had been thinking about it for probably a year and a half and I had already introduced the subject to my readers who went [gasp] no, no, don’t do it.

Because they were older subscribers and they were kind of scared of the whole idea and they didn’t understand — they liked having a print paper. And I like having a print paper. You know my own preference is to have a print paper. But as a small publication’s editor I have had so many problems with the post office because of lost issues which have to be replaced at first class rates, you know. So if they screwed up a delivery or damaged it or had late delivery, which happened time after time where people would call up and it would be the 15th of the month and they’d eventually — I mean I would publish on the 21st of the month with the idea hopefully that they would get it by the first of the month. A lot of people wouldn’t get it until the 15th, maybe the 20th. And they would call up and say I didn’t get it. So I would send out a duplicate issue at first class rates and they would get two, that’s right. The interesting thing is very often they’d get the two on the same day. Now what does that tell you? It tells you that the post office, the carrier was either sitting on it or, in many cases, reading it. Because when they would get the first one the tab would be broken. I cannot tell you how often that happened. And so it cost a fortune to be replacing these issues, plus the international mail is a tremendous headache to prepare. I knew more about the mailing requirements than the post office did so in some cases I would have to take the pages from the international mail manual with me when I © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

would bring the bags of international mail, and say no, this is really the way periodicals postage is supposed to be prepared and sent. This is how the tags have to be. Just a tremendous amount of work. And then paper prices keep going up. So there was that. And then I had some health problems where I thought okay I’m just going to tell the subscribers I can’t do these all-nighters again and again and again and again. So once I told them that they said oh, we love you, see?
They were wonderful and just like that they’ve just been converting.
So they subscribe but now they’re going to access it —

Yeah. And so the first online issue came out this last week. I’d wanted to do it by the first but I had to convert so many people plus we re-formatted The Rag from a tabloid to an 8– 1/2 by 11 so that they can read it and print it easily, and they can read it easier on the screen and they can print it off. I mean you can print off a tabloid on 8–1/2 by 11 but the type is this itsy bitsy you know. So we reformatted it plus I can use the color. So that was good. And then also we redesigned the website. So I’ve actually been doing all-nighters since I said I’m going to put out the last issue in October. Well and then also I downsized the office by two-thirds. So I haven’t gotten any sleep yet, that’s why I took a nap this afternoon. So it’s just plugging away, and then the on-line distributor had to set certain things in motion while we did this conversion. So it actually, the first one was delivered to subscribers on Wednesday. And I talked to my sister who is monitoring all of this back home in Minnesota and she said wow, people love it. They’re finding it easy to download and they love the color.
